Article Title: Another Punjab MP faces SIR trouble; ECI clarifies Dharamvira Gandhi’s name ‘very much there’
Article Text:
ECI rejects Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday rejected Congress leader and Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim that his name and those of his family members were missing from Punjab's draft electoral roll published on August 13.According to an ECI statement, the Lok Sabha member and four of his family members are listed as electors in the Patiala Assembly constituency."Dr Dharamvira Gandhi, Member of Parliament, as well as his family members, wife Jagdamba Kaushal, daughter Rohani Prashar, daughter-in-law Chahat Sahuja, and son Nabendhu, are very much a part of the Draft Electoral Roll published on 13th August 2026. They are registered as electors in AC No 115 – Patiala, Part No 98, at Serial numbers 44 to 48," the poll panel said.The ECI’s clarification came a day after Dharamvira Gandhi, who was earlier associated with Punjab’s ruling AAP, claimed that his name and those of his family members were missing from the draft electoral roll published as part of the ECI’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in the state, where Assembly elections are due in February 2027.His claim came on the same day that BJP leader Raghav Chadha, another Punjab MP and another former AAP member, was marked as “shifted” in the state’s draft electoral roll. Chadha, who joined the BJP in April, accused his former party of "political vendetta." AAP rejected the allegation, pointing out that the SIR exercise is conducted by the Election Commission and not by a state government.Earlier, former diplomat Navdeep Suri had also alleged that he faced "difficulties" in “establishing my citizenship” during the Punjab SIR.
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday rejected Congress leader and Patiala MP Dharamvira Gandhi's claim that his name and those of his family members were missing from Punjab's draft electoral roll. According to an ECI statement, the Lok Sabha member and four of hisFamily members are listed as electors in the PatialA Assembly constituency.

Article Title: IndiGo aircraft hits parking stand pole at Srinagar airport
Article Text:
Srinagar: Ground staff attend to an IndiGo aircraft after flight 6E 225 (VT-NOG), operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar, hit a pole while being parked at Srinagar airport (PTI Photo).

MUMBAI: An IndiGo aircraft operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar came into contact with a parking stand pole while parking at Srinagar International Airport on Friday, shortly after landing. The aircraft departed Navi Mumbai at 6.50am and landed in Srinagar at 9.25am.IndiGo, in a statement, said all passengers and crew were safe and had deplaned from the aircraft. The relevant authorities were immediately informed, and an investigation is underway. The aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance and will resume operations after securing the required clearances.
Article Summary: An IndiGo aircraft operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar came into contact with a parking stand pole. All passengers and crew were safe and had deplaned from the aircraft. The aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance and will resume operations after securing the required clearances.

Article Title: PM Modi congratulates 'friend' Meloni on becoming longest-serving postwar Italian PM

PM Modi congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday congratulated his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, a day after she become Italy's longest continuously serving prime minister since the post- World War II era.In a post on X, PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni."Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership," the prime minister wrote."Her friendship has also been instrumental in advancing the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and I look forward to continuing our close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of our countries. My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead," he added.The two leaders' widely known friendship is often referred to as "Melodi" - a combination of their surnames.Meloni, who has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, is the first woman to hold that position.On Thursday, her conservative administration marked 1,413 uninterrupted days in office, making it Italy's longest-serving continuous government since World War II and surpassing the record previously set by late former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi from 2001 to 2005.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni on her 1,413 days in office. PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni. Meloni has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, is the first woman to hold that position.

Article Title: HarperCollins to publish Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir
Article Text:
HarperCollins to publish former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir after Penguin backs out

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: So, who does Sonia Gandhi’s controversial memoir ‘Belonging’ belong to? HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir, ending weeks of uncertainty over who would carry the domestic edition after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) exited the deal over some changes to the text. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release.Billed as one of the most anticipated political memoirs in recent years, Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging, offering an insider's perspective on India's political journey through Gandhi's own eyes.The HarperCollins announcement comes on the heels of a public controversy over PRHI's departure from the project, which Congress leaders have framed as an act of political censorship. Party leader Ashok Gehlot alleged that pressure had been exerted on Penguin to edit out sections dealing with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the RSS, and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's tenure, calling the episode a "murder of democracy.Penguin pushed back on that framing, maintaining that it retained the right to fact-check manuscripts and suggest edits to authors, and said it remained open to publishing the book.The company had earlier this year also halted distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's The Once and Future Riot, about the Muzaffarnagar riots — a decision critics have pointed to as part of a pattern.Adding a layer of intrigue to the row was the fact that Alfred A. Knopf, the memoir's American publisher, is itself a Penguin Random House imprint — raising the question, as Gehlot put it, of why a version cleared for global release would need alteration for Indian readers. "What is the reason, or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?" he asked.
Article Summary: HarperCollins India has stepped in to publish the Congress leader’s memoir. The book will hit Indian shelves on November 10, 2026 — the same day as its international release. Belonging is described as a personal account of love, identity, duty and belonging.

Article Title: Use of drugs serious concern, act on it quickly, AAIB to DGCA on AI Phuket-Delhi flight interim report
Article Text:
The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” in its preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026. While the probe is still on, the prelim report officially confirms that the “confirmatory (dope) test report of the pilot-in-command (PIC) was found non-negative” and that the Airbus A320 had suffered an extremely rare multiple hydraulic failure.When the “event” occurred, “initially, (the aircraft) gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet…. seat belt signs were off. Consequently, some passengers and cabin crew suffered injuries,” the report says. The “event’s” impact on the aircraft cabin damage was such that a “lavatory commode was uprooted from its original location.”The report says in its conclusion: “Detailed investigation regarding technical and other aspects are underway. In this case, it has been observed that the PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test. The confirmation of use of psycho-active substances is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority.The preliminary report is published as per ICAO guidelines. The investigation is in progress. The final report will be published in due course.”The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.“At 04:02:43 UTC, while cruising at flight level 36,000 feet, the aircraft’s flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of green hydraulic system. Further, at 04:02:47 UTC, the flight control system detected loss of blue and yellow hydraulic systems. At 04:02:48 UTC, the autopilot got disengaged and a continuous repetitive chime (CRC) came. At 04:02:51 UTC, the Stall warning triggered for 2 seconds.”“The co-pilot, who was the pilot flying (PF), responded and tried to control the prevailing situation. Subsequently, PIC took over the controls. Meanwhile, the aircraft encountered an altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet during the event. At around 04:02:52 UTC, the blue hydraulic system was recovered, and few seconds later, the yellow hydraulic and the green hydraulic systems were also recovered. Consequently, this led to the recovery of the flight control surfaces. Subsequently, the aircraft operation returned to its normal operating condition,” says the report.The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the "muscles" that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels. The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the “muscles” that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheelsThe cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and cabin crew. The flight crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision to continue the flight to its destination, Delhi and not divert to the nearest en route airport.The aircraft cabin suffered significant damage during the “event”. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit (PSU) panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken, and the sealing panel was found dislocated near the 10th row. The forward right-side emergency exit handle was found broken.In a statement, Air India said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India's highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements.Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.”“The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements and will take appropriate action wherever warranted. Air India remains committed to implementing any recommendations arising from the investigation,” AI said.
Article Summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” The preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday warned that anti-national and anti-social forces seeking to spread hatred or undermine India's unity would face consequences, invoking Lord Krishna's message on the occasion of Janmashtami.Addressing a gathering in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, on the second day of his visit, Adityanath emphasised that His teachings and message remained equally relevant today."Wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. Article Title: Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: The preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet, triggering an autopilot disengagement, stall warning and an altitude upset. Alongside the technical findings, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has recommended that the DGCA take action against the Pilot-in-Command, who tested non-negative for psychoactive substance use following the flight."The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority," the report said. The interim safety recommendation asked the regulator to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psycho-active substance." Post-flight, both pilots underwent a breath analyser test, which came back satisfactory. But the subsequent psychoactive substance detection test returned a non-negative result for the PIC, a finding confirmed by a follow-up laboratory blood test. The co-pilot tested negative on both counts.The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window.VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region. At 04:02:43 UTC, the flight control system "detected loss of green hydraulic system." Four seconds later, the flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems. With all three systems compromised simultaneously, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet from its assigned level, the report said.The co-pilot, who was Pilot Flying, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift. "At around 04:02:52 UTC, the Blue hydraulic system was recovered, and a few seconds later, the Yellow hydraulic and the Green hydraulic systems were also recovered," the report said. It restored normal flight control surfaces within seconds of the failure.But with seatbelt signs off during cruise, the sudden upset threw passengers and crew around the cabin. Twenty-four people, including four cabin crew, needed medical attention on landing; four were hospitalised with serious injuries. The cabin damage was extensive: cracked ceiling panels across multiple rows, dislodged overhead bins, a broken emergency exit handle, a lavatory commode "uprooted from its original location," and a bent crew seat. Despite the injuries, the flight crew chose not to divert, opting instead to continue to Delhi while requesting medical priority from ATC. The aircraft landed safely on runway 11L at 05:30 UTC, around ninety minutes after the failure.Investigators have already flagged one detail for closer scrutiny: the aircraft was dispatched from Phuket under an active Minimum Equipment List item for the Power Transfer Unit, invoked a week earlier on July 28. The PTU serves as an auxiliary hydraulic source shared between the green and yellow systems, and its status at the time of the failure is expected to be a focus of the ongoing probe. Flight recorder data has been downloaded and is under analysis, and a technical team from Airbus and France's BEA inspected the aircraft in Delhi in mid-August, after which hydraulic components and fluid samples were removed for further testing.“The Airbus A320 aircraft has three hydraulic systems. They are identified as the green, blue and yellow systems. Together they supply hydraulic power at 3000 psi (206 bar) to the main power users. Services which are not used during flight are isolated from the main supply. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another. Each system has its own hydraulic reservoir,” the report said, explaining the hydraulics on the aircraft.On the green system, the normal source of pressure is the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) located on the left engine and, as an auxiliary source, the Power Transfer Unit (PTU). On the blue system, the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump) and, as an auxiliary source, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT). On the yellow system, the normal source of pressure is the EDP located on the right engine and as auxiliary sources the PTU and the electric pump (E-Pump). “Each hydraulic system pressurisation information is available for the aircraft systems through one pressure transmitter (numerical value of the pressure), two pressure switches (discrete value indicating if there is a loss of pressure). Relevant Hydraulic components were removed from the aircraft for further analysis,” the report said. The PTU is an auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems without transfer of fluid between the two systems. It operates automatically if there is a delta pressure of 500 psi between the green/yellow or yellow/green hydraulic systems, it addedThe said report is preliminary, and a detailed technical investigation is still underway.
Article Summary: Preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet. Autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet.

Article Title: India, Belgium deepen defence, clean-energy ties; to double trade
Article Text:
India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade

New Delhi: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade within five years as PM Modi held talks with Belgian counterpart Bart De Wever, the first Belgian PM to visit India in nearly two decades, reports Sachin Parashar.Following the talks, Modi pitched India's 7.8% growth in the last quarter as an opportunity for the world. In a joint statement with De Wever, Modi said global conflicts were causing major upheaval, disrupting food, fuel and supply chains, and creating uncertainty across sectors."Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world," said Modi.PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries.Belgium accounted for $4.2bn of FDI inflows from April 2000 to Dec 2025, making it the 18th-largest source of FDI into India. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development, and another five announcements, including appointment of a defence attache in Indian embassy in Brussels.Asked whether there was any discussion on pending extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, who remains in a Belgium jail, MEA secretary Sibi George said law enforcement cooperation was an “important topic of discussion and an important aspect of the relationship with Belgium”.“All issues of concern and interest are discussed at all levels of our engagement ... India remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to the country to face the law,” he added.Modi said ties with Belgium had expanded beyond traditional sectors. “Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries,” said the PM. “The agreements between our govts and defence industries will open up opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between our agencies to combat crime,” he added.PM said unprecedented cooperation, including the recently concluded FTA between India and EU – two of the world’s largest democratic blocs – would give a boost to global stability, development and shared prosperity.The leaders also discussed Ukraine and West Asia, underlining their support for the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. In a joint statement, they stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts aimed at an early end to conflicts and the restoration of peace,” the PM added.The leaders called for closer partnerships in semiconductor technologies to create resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries, with Modi saying that Belgium’s expertise in semiconductors and India’s scale complement each other.The two leaders agreed to soon conclude a migration and mobility agreement to facilitate talent mobility.Belgium also expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. De Wever condemned the attack on civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. “Both leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with the law,” said the statement.The leaders also focused on clean energy, critical minerals and reliable supply chains. “The MoU on Renewable Energy signed today will give momentum to our sustainability cooperation. In critical minerals, we have decided to enhance ties in processing & recycling,” PM said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development.

Article Title: Isro’s GSLV-F17 successfully places EOS-05 Earth observation satellite in geosynchronous orbit
Article Text:
ISRO’s GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission successfully accomplished

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRIHARIKOTA: The Indian Space Research Organisation ( Isro ) successfully launched EOS-05, India’s first imaging satellite designed to operate from a geosynchronous orbit, aboard GSLV-F17 in the early hours of Friday.The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at Sriharikota at 2.55am and placed the around 2,367kg Earth observation satellite in its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.This was the 19th GSLV flight. GSLV-F17 had a S139 solid core with four L40H liquid strap-ons, a GL40HT liquid second stage and a CUS15 indigenous cryogenic upper stage, besides a four-metre composite ogive payload fairing.EOS-05 was injected into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a nominal perigee of 171km, apogee of 31026km and inclination of 19.28 degrees. The satellite will be moved to the final orbit through a series of manoeuvres using onboard thrusters.Isro chairman V Narayanan said the rocket injected the satellite in the intended orbit precisely. This is the 107th launch from Sriharikota and 19th GSLV flight. The chairman addressed from the mission control complex post launch."From launching 1536kg payload in the first GSLV launch, the chairman said the rocket has carried the heaviest payload in its history at 2367kg. We gradually improved the performance of the vehicle by optimising the structural mass and improving propulsion system. The satellite is India's first dedicating imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit. It will provide strategic data."The chairman also said Isro will have six more launches this financial year including navigation satellite NVS-03 and Gaganyaan first uncrewed mission.India had 21 operational Earth observation satellites as of February 2026. Of these, most are in low-Earth or sun-synchronous polar orbits, while India’s geostationary-orbit Earth observation capability is currently represented by the meteorological satellites INSAT-3D, INSAT-3DR and INSAT-3DS. EOS-05 is India’s first imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit.The launch was the first GSLV mission since GSLV-F16 successfully placed the joint Nasa-Isro NISAR Earth observation satellite in a 743km sun-synchronous orbit on July 30, 2025. Friday’s launch was Isro’s second orbital mission of 2026. The first, PSLV-C62 carrying EOS-N1 and other payloads on Jan 12, failed following an anomaly towards the end of the rocket’s third-stage flight.
Article Summary: EOS-05 is India’s first imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit. The 51.7-metre-tall, 420.5-tonne, three-stage rocket lifted off from the second launch pad at 2.55am.

Article Title: Watch: 2 workers make it out alive 9 days after Nepal floods hit hydropower tunnel
Article Text:
The rescue of two workers have revived hope for hundreds of others still said to be trapped

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be prioritized in Nepal's recovery plan? Infrastructure rebuilding Financial aid for affected families Long-term disaster preparedness Environmental restoration 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and landslides trapped hundreds of workers inside tunnels across several hydropower sites.The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further after rescuers heard voices coming from inside the tunnel, according to Bipin Regmi, police chief in the flood-hit district of Nuwakot.“Rescuers heard voices,” Regmi told CNN, adding that a medical team was on its way to the site.The two workers were pulled out in quick succession from inside the Trishuli 3A plant, where rescuers have been boring into a tunnel in an effort to reach 42 workers who had remained unaccounted for.Video showed about a dozen rescuers pulling one man through a small opening in the ground and clapping as he emerged. The mud-covered worker was then carried away on a rescuer’s shoulder, while a medical team checked on him.Nepal Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first rescue during the operation. Nepal lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane later said a second worker had also been rescued alive.The tunnel leading to the underground powerhouse is more than 4 kilometres (2.5 miles) long.Dozens of workers were inside when the catastrophic flooding hit the area.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, according to local authorities, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped inside tunnels. Among those unaccounted for are workers from China, South Korea and India.Read more: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery cost The rescue effort has continued under treacherous conditions since Aug. 26, when massive floods and landslides tore through parts of Nepal, likely after a glacier collapse. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.On the Tibet side of the border, China said late Wednesday that 21 people had been killed and 541 were missing.The chances of finding survivors have become increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Indian Army Colonel Parikshit Mehra, who was involved in the rescue operation at the Trishuli 3A site, said earlier this week that the first 48 hours are the most crucial in a tunnel rescue.“People who are stuck tend to panic much more than when they are outside in the open,” Mehra told CNN’s Anderson Cooper.“Getting stuck in a tunnel you can’t see anything. Generally if you stay in the dark you get disoriented in about 24-25 hours,” he said.“Beyond that, (after) 48 hours, you start hallucinating. And then I think from there on it’s always a fight.”Yet, even as the operation entered its ninth day, Mehra offered a note of hope saying, “There have been miracles.”Also read: Nepal minister goes back on flash flood 'compensation' claim The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, caused widespread destruction across northern and central Nepal, killing at least 1,282 people and leaving thousands missing. Nepal Police said the highest number of recovered bodies were reported from Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and West, Nuwakot and Rasuwa, with rescue and recovery operations continuing across the affected areas.
Article Summary: Rescuers pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday. The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing.

Article Title: PM Modi takes stock of flood situation in Varanasi as water crosses warning mark
Article Text:
The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall.PM Modi, who is also the Member of Parliament from Varanasi, sought detailed information from the district magistrate about the river's water level and the arrangements being made at relief camps for people affected by the floods.The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected and ensure that all necessary facilities are made available immediately.He also instructed officials to make immediate arrangements wherever there is an additional requirement for relief material and expedite relief work for affected people.PM Modi further directed the administration to maintain constant vigilance over the flood situation and relief operations and ensure that immediate assistance reaches those affected.The Prime Minister's intervention came as the Ganga continued to rise in Varanasi.According to the Central Water Commission (CWC), the river's water level reached 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site at 6 am on Thursday, crossing the warning level of 70.262 metres. The water level was rising at a rate of 2 cm per hour.The danger level at the site is 71.262 metres, while the highest flood level is 73.901 metres.The district administration has been closely monitoring areas affected by the rising waters of the Ganga and Varuna rivers. On Tuesday, District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar and Varanasi Police Commissioner Mohit Agrawal inspected several flood-affected areas after travelling by an NDRF boat from Namo Ghat.The officials visited Salarpur, Saraiya, Konia, Pul Kohna, Dhelvaria and Sarai Mohana to assess waterlogging and the situation of residents. They also interacted with affected people and assured them of all possible assistance.The district magistrate directed officials to remain on high alert and keep arrangements ready to shift residents to safer locations. He also ordered that boats and other resources remain available for relief and rescue operations.Relief camps at the Primary School in Salarpur and Vidya Vihar Inter College were also inspected. Officials were directed to ensure adequate food, drinking water, electricity, lighting, sanitation, healthcare and security, with special attention to children, women and elderly people.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi spoke to Varanasi District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar. He took stock of the flood situation in the city as the rising water level of the Ganga crossed the warning mark amid incessant rainfall. The Prime Minister directed the district administration to work on a war footing to provide relief to those affected.

Article Title: ‘Hit him because he was speaking wrong’: Ganesh mandal worker after slapping anti-noise activist in Pune
Article Text:
An anti-noise campaigner was assaulted on Tilak Road in Pune





PUNE: Anti-noise campaigner Vidyanand Bapat of Narayan Peth was assaulted on Tilak Road on Thursday allegedly by a member of a Kothrud-based Ganesh mandal, amid a simmering debate over the use of DJs and high-decibel sound systems during Ganeshotsav.The accused, identified as Santosh Chavan, president of Kothrud-based Janjagruti Pratishthan, was taken into custody soon after the incident. The Vishrambaug police later registered an FIR under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) and 353(2) (statements promoting enmity/hatred) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , who also holds the home portfolio, strongly condemned the assault, saying every citizen had the right to express views. “Police have arrested the accused. In a city like Pune, such disputes should not turn violent. I have said earlier too that we should return Ganeshotsav celebrations to the traditional way. We may not achieve complete success in the first year, but we must make a sincere effort to reach that goal over time,” Fadnavis said.Deputy CM Eknath Shinde echoed the sentiment, saying the festival must be celebrated without causing inconvenience to residents. “Ganesh festival is an integral part of our tradition, and we must ensure that it is celebrated in a manner that preserves its essence. Nothing should be done that creates problems for local residents or causes inconvenience to people,” Shinde said.A video of the alleged attack that surfaced online showed Chavan challenging Bapat over his opposition to DJs and sound systems during Ganeshotsav and questioning his authority to speak on behalf of Pune residents. In the clip, Chavan is heard admitting to the assault, saying, “I assaulted him because he was speaking wrong.”Defending his action later, Chavan told reporters that Bapat was selectively targeting Ganeshotsav despite several other civic issues facing the city.Bapat, however, dismissed the attack as an attempt at “cheap publicity” and declared that it would not deter his campaign against noise pollution. “The attacker was like a zombie and there is no point arguing with such people. Police should do their job and take action against him. I know that what I am doing is right, so there is no question of stepping back,” he said.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the accused had been detained and stressed that violence could not be justified under any circumstances. “Everyone has the freedom of speech. Violence is not justified,” Kumar said, adding that stringent action would follow.Kumar said Bapat had been provided round-the-clock police protection until further orders. Regarding a complaint filed against Bapat, Kumar said police were conducting an inquiry.Deputy police commissioner Krushikesh Rawale said Chavan has a criminal record, with at least two cases registered against him in 2014 and 2015. “Following the attack, we conducted a threat assessment and, based on the analysis, provided Bapat with security. One police security officer has been assigned to him, while guards have also been deployed outside his residence,” he said, adding that the security arrangement would be reviewed daily and a decision on its continuation would be taken accordingly.BJP corporator and PMC leader of the house Ganesh Bidkar said state govt had taken serious note of the incident. “BJP will ensure that Bapat is not harmed,” he said.The attack triggered widespread condemnation across party lines. Baramati MP Supriya Sule said ideological disagreements could never justify violence. “Responding to ideological differences with violence is a method that in no way benefits Maharashtra’s cultured and progressive tradition,” she said, stressing that everyone had the right to express an opinion in a democratic system.Union minister Murlidhar Mohol also denounced the assault, saying differences should be resolved through dialogue and debate, not physical attacks. “If we do not agree with someone’s position, it can be addressed through dialogue and by presenting an alternative viewpoint. Physical attack on a person for expressing his or her views is not the right way,” Mohol said.Congress state president Harshwardhan Sapkal, Congress member Prashant Jagtap and NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar joined the criticism. “If the price of ideological differences is beatings and arrests, then the coming times are truly going to be very tough,” Sapkal posted on X.Jagtap described the attack as an assault on Pune citizens who consistently raised concerns over loudspeakers and noise pollution.Following the incident, NCP (SP) workers, activists and citizens supporting Bapat staged a protest outside Vishrambaug police station. Bapat has emerged as a prominent voice in Pune’s ongoing debate over noise pollution during Ganeshotsav. He had earlier objected to the use of DJs and large sound systems at a Pune Municipal Corporation meeting, leading to a heated confrontation with representatives of Ganesh mandals and his eventual escort from the venue amid slogans and protests.Workers of Ganesh mandals condemned the attack on Bapat, saying such an attack was not acceptable.
Article Summary: Anti-noise campaigner Vidyanand Bapat of Narayan Peth was assaulted on Tilak Road in Pune. The accused, identified as Santosh Chavan, president of Kothrud- based Janjagruti Pratishthan, was taken into custody soon after the incident. The Vishrambaug police later registered an FIR under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt) and 126 (wrongful restraint)

Article Title: Estonia minister quits after €70-million Ukraine shell deal involving Indian firm
Article Text:
Estonia minister quits in India-linked row

Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine using €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company, Euronews reported.It emerged on Wednesday that Estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress reported that in 2024, Estonia signed a shell-supply deal with Italian-registered Datasel, owned by Indian company Neco Defence Munitions.Neither company had previously manufactured shells.The 2024 deal is now being challenged by Estonia in an arbitration case.Pevkur, who has been defence minister since 2022, said he was taking political responsibility for the controversy.“Although the minister does not count socks and ammunition or conduct contract negotiations, the National Audit Office’s criticisms, primarily concerning the activities of the Defence Forces and the Centre for Defence Investments, raise the question of political responsibility,” Pevkur said.The minister said he had not read the contracts, as defence ministers do not usually handle individual arms deals.“The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations. The defence minister does not count socks and ammunition,” Pevkur said, adding: “The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine.”Pevkur’s resignation comes as the Russia-Ukraine war has already lasted longer than World War I, with no clear signs of peace or a return to normalcy.
Article Summary: Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine. The deal involved €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company. Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.

Article Title: To impart nationalistic learning, Bengal to have 1,000 RSS-run schools within a year: Suvendu
Article Text:
Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS

KOLKATA: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati in every district, municipality and panchayat within a year. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education.Adhikari, who spoke at an event to mark the 74th anniversary of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture, urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning". He invited its brass to the secretariat to meet officials and take the initiative forward.Bengal has 313 such schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras. The CM said he wanted the organisation to focus on establishing more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, alleging that "more anti-national activities take place" in these districts. The erstwhile TMC govt, he said, polluted the education environment and institutions like Vidya Bharati would need to "help the state come out of this".He accused TMC of even twisting the Bengali syllabus to divide people. "Mother was referred to as 'amma' and not 'ma'... The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's or Swami Vivekananda's lessons remained neglected..."Invoking Syama Prasad Mookerjee's call of "ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan", the CM said it would apply to education, too. "We won't allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities, while another department will look after Aliah University," he said. Aliah University is currently managed by the state's minority affairs department. "I felicitated the board toppers. Later, the minority affairs department sent a separate file containing the names of 27 Muslim students. I asked why? ... I have already felicitated 20 students, and they include Muslims, Jains and Buddhists."Anand Rao, a Vidya Bharati official, told TOI its schools train students in "bharatiyatwa (Indianness)" as well as puja rituals. Some run till Class 5, others up to classes 8, 10 and 12.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan states its vision is "to develop a system of education which would help build a younger generation committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour".
Article Summary: Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target Thursday to establish at least 1,000 schools run by RSS's education wing Vidya Bharati. He also suggested a plan to merge the state's four education departments into one, specifying that there would be no separate administration for madrassa education. He urged the body to shoulder the responsibility of imparting what he termed "nationalistic learning"

Article Title: China’s grey-zone game: Why India must prepare for ‘armed coexistence’
Article Text:
India-China ties have thawed since the border skirmish in 2020.

Former foreign secretary

Vijay Gokhale

argues that China waits for a strategic opening, acts pre-emptively and then builds a narrative of self-defence.

His new book, “China’s Wars: The Politics and Diplomacy Behind its Military Coercion”, examines past conflicts and China’s recent grey-zone tactics.

In an interview with Indrajeet Rai, Gokhale explains why the

India-China relationship

has entered an era of “armed coexistence”, why a full-scale war is not the most likely outcome but cannot be ruled out, and how political uncertainty after Xi Jinping could produce global economic shocks or military adventurism.

You describe China as an opportunistic power. What does that mean, and when does Beijing decide to act pre-emptively?

China often depicts its own aggressive action as defensive and blames the other side. How central is this narrative warfare to its strategy?

China’s grey-zone strategy seeks to steadily pressure and exhaust rivals while avoiding the escalation of tensions into full-scale war.

You argue that China is pursuing sustained grey-zone coercion. How does this work against India?

Does that mean a large-scale India-China war is unlikely in the foreseeable future?

China’s capabilities against Taiwan have grown, while the US is distracted by several conflicts. Could Xi Jinping move on Taiwan to secure his legacy?

Xi has removed the age and term limits that helped institutionalise succession. What happens after him and why should India worry?

China has few formal allies and did little visibly to support Iran. Does it lack the partnerships needed to become a global leader?

As US-China rivalry intensifies, which side of the emerging world order should India prefer?

Edited excerpts:By opportunistic power, I did not intend to suggest that China is very different from other major powers. In the case studies in my book, China waited for the international situation to turn favourable, or for some advantage to accrue from its relations with other major powers, before carrying out conflict with a neighbour or another country. It used opportunity strategically to achieve its goals.The Chinese idea of preventive deterrence or preventive conflict differs from the Western concept. In the West, deterrence is a counteraction intended to stop the adversary from escalating. In the Chinese context, it is pre-emptive: China acts even before the adversary has had the chance to act first. The aim is to deliver a political and psychological shock so the adversary desists or fears retaliation.The 1962 conflict is one example. There was no indication that India intended to launch a military assault. But China used the words of then PM Jawaharlal Nehru and an international situation dominated by the Cuban missile crisis to act pre-emptively against India.The Chinese Communist Party utilised China’s difficult circumstances after the collapse of the empire and projected itself as the only organisation capable of pulling the country out of its problems. It placed the blame for China’s declining economy and global influence on external circumstances. It played the victim’s card: China was perennially the victim, and the party was the instrument that would restore it as a major power.The blame, therefore, was always placed on somebody else: The colonial powers, the United States in the Korean War, India in the 1962 war and the Soviet Union in the 1969 conflict. There was never an acknowledgement that some responsibility also fell on China.This is not limited to foreign policy. The party does not take responsibility for major domestic failures either: The Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution or the 1989 Tiananmen incident. Blame falls on an external force or a few bad elements, never the party itself.Since 1979, China has not fought a real conflict. The leadership made economic development the priority, and successive leaders after Mao Zedong focused on reform and opening up.But China was not willing to give up the use of force; it changed the manner in which force was used. Instead of hot wars or major conflict, it engaged and continues to engage in very low-intensity military conflict, popularly known as grey-zone warfare.Grey-zone warfare uses threats or actual force while staying below the threshold that might tempt the rival to launch a counteroffensive. It punishes or deters, but stops short of making the rival feel compelled to push back with force. We see it along the Line of Actual Control, in the South China Sea and in the East China Sea.I have characterised the situation on the LAC after 2020 as the end of peaceful coexistence and the beginning of armed coexistence. Armed coexistence does not mean conflict. It means China will continue to take grey-zone military action around the LAC to keep us tied down and to exhaust us not only financially - because keeping forces and equipment at those heights costs a lot - but also in terms of men and material.This fulfils a key Chinese objective: Keeping India confined to South Asia.Apart from the United States, there are few potential rivals in this century, and India is one. If you look at India, it's geographical location, its population size, its territorial size, its talent, it's economic potential. All of it lends a credence to the belief that India can become a major power in this century. And clearly, China would like to delay that possibility.Nobody can predict this definitively. China and its decision-making processes are opaque, and there are no alternative channels of information such as free media or civil society.China is a mature state focused on becoming the strongest economy and power in the world. On a rational cost-benefit analysis, the price of a major war with India could exceed the benefits. Logically, China would be reluctant to engage in such a conflict.At the end of the day, however, it is impossible to predict. We have to be prepared for the worst, while logically understanding that a hot conflict with India may not be in China’s interest in the foreseeable future.An American commander of the Indo-Pacific Command, Admiral Philip Davidson, suggested that by 2027 China would have the military capability to launch an assault on Taiwan. Some interpreted that to mean China would attack by 2027, but he did not actually say this.China’s capabilities for an assault on an island have substantially increased: Landing craft, area-denial capabilities, communication systems and anti-ship missiles.It is one thing for a major power to bomb another country and destroy its infrastructure, and quite another to occupy or conquer it. That requires a very large commitment of forces and material, with no assured guarantee of victory.China’s demographic decline is already causing anxiety. An assault would mean mass casualties because boots on the ground would be required. After Galwan, India acknowledged within days that 20 soldiers had been martyred; China took much longer to admit fatalities. With Taiwan potentially producing casualties in the hundreds or thousands, Beijing will worry about the domestic impact.This is where democracy, for all its weaknesses, becomes a strength. A democratic government has electoral and constitutional legitimacy to act, including in war. In China, the party claims it has popular support but has never tested that proposition. The reaction to large-scale war casualties is unpredictable.Deng Xiaoping introduced two reforms that stabilised succession: Those above 68 could not continue in top party positions, and the president was limited to two five-year terms. This helped ensure smooth transitions from Jiang Zemin to Hu Jintao and then to Xi Jinping.Xi has abolished the age and term limits. In an authoritarian system, no leader will voluntarily give up power because enemies may find it easier to target him, and he cannot be certain a successor will not misuse authority against him.China could enter a period of political uncertainty and potentially turmoil as Xi ages and factions emerge in a contest for power. It is unclear whether this happens before or after his death, or whether he intends to stand for a fourth term.Because China is the world’s second-largest economy, domestic turmoil would affect its economy, military and diplomacy and create huge ripple effects abroad. Beleaguered regimes also sometimes use an external threat to divert attention. India must consider whether turmoil could produce military adventurism and how to preserve its national interests, sovereignty and territorial integrity.China lacks the United States’ large network of treaty allies. But we should not underestimate the goodwill it enjoys. The Belt and Road Initiative has been welcomed as an alternative route to development. Western assistance often came with harsh conditions; China offers fewer and less onerous strings. Nobody gives aid for free, but China has built substantial diplomatic influence.There was little need for China to do more in the Iran war. It could neither persuade the United States to stop nor force peace. It protected its oil interests and relations with Iran and the Gulf countries without entering the mediation game.When the conflict ends, Iran will rebuild using its oil and gas wealth. It is unlikely to trust the West, while China can build infrastructure at a scale few others can match. China needs energy; Iran needs infrastructure and money. That creates an enormous downstream economic opportunity and a win-win situation. Why would China get significantly involved now when there seems to be no clear way out of the conflict?India should not look at the world order through an either-or lens. The United States and China will both remain major powers. The question is how, in a triangular or quadrangular relationship, including the European Union if it acts as a union, we create an international framework relevant to this century.India has objective advantages: Its location, demographics and consumer base; tested political stability; an independent military capability and growing defence industry; and talent.I do not see how India can fail to become a major power in this century. The international order is disintegrating and all states are hedging their bets; India is doing so too. The task is not to choose a US-led or China-led order. It is to help build an order in which India is one of the leaders.
Article Summary: Vijay Gokhale argues that China waits for a strategic opening, acts pre- emptively and then builds a narrative of self-defence. His new book, “China’s Wars: The Politics and Diplomacy Behind its Military Coercion’, examines past conflicts and China‘s recent grey-zone tactics.

Article Title: 'Outstanding achievement': PM Modi hails Isro after successful EOS-05 launch
Article Text:
The Prime Minister also highlighted the expanding role of Indian industry in the country's space programme. He said the growing partnership with ISRO was helping strengthen the sector and broaden India's capabilities.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday lauded the Indian Space Research Organisation ISRO ) after the successful launch of the GSLV-F17 rocket carrying the advanced Earth Observation Satellite-05 (EOS-05), calling the mission an “outstanding achievement” and a proud moment for the nation.The satellite was launched by Isro from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday aboard the GSLV-F17. The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg EOS-05 into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit (Sub-GTO), marking another major milestone for India’s space programme.“Yet another outstanding achievement by ISRO and a proud moment for our nation. The successful launch of GSLV-F17 carrying EOS-05, India’s first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit is a reflection of the excellence, innovation and growing capabilities that define India’s space sector," PM Modi said in a post on X.The Prime Minister also highlighted the expanding role of Indian industry in the country's space programme. He said the growing partnership with ISRO was helping strengthen the sector and broaden India's capabilities."The growing partnership between ISRO and Indian industry is adding new strength and scale to our space programme and expanding India’s capabilities across the entire space ecosystem," he added.Isro chief V Narayanan described the mission as a significant achievement for India's space programme. He said the satellite was in good health after being injected into orbit.“I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the Advanced Earth Observation Satellite 05, the geo-imaging satellite, in the intended and required orbit," he said.Narayanan said EOS-05 would become India's first dedicated imaging satellite operating from a geosynchronous orbit once it is operationalised. The satellite is expected to provide important strategic data for the country.“Today, we have injected the heaviest satellite, 2367 kgs, using this launch vehicle. The health of the satellite is perfectly alright,” the ISRO chief said.The GSLV-F17 mission was the 19th flight of India's geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle. It was launched from the second launch pad at Sriharikota and carried EOS-05 towards a sub-GTO.The mission adds to India's growing earth observation capabilities while highlighting the increasing technological strength of its space programme.
Article Summary: The satellite was launched by Isro from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday. The rocket precisely placed the 2,367-kg EOS-05 into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit (Sub-GTO)

Article Title: Chirag Paswan vs Jitan Manjhi in Bihar: SC 'creamy layer' debate divides NDA; will it open up a Pandora's box?
Article Text:
Chirag vs Manjhi: SC ‘creamy layer’ debate puts Bihar NDA unity to test.

Turf war for Dalit leadership in Bihar

Manjhi has accused Chirag Paswan of seeking to maintain 'Dusadh dominance'.

Homogeneous group vs categorisation

Chirag Paswan demanded resignation of Manjhi and his son Santosh Kumar Suman.

Two-fold challenge

'BJP testing people's mood'

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support economic criteria over caste-based reservations? Yes, it should be prioritised for fairness. No, caste discrimination needs to be addressed first. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Could the open sparring over “quota within quota” between two prominent Dalit faces of Bihar last month open up a Pandora’s box for the BJP-led NDA government? Union ministers Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived Dalit sections.Manjhi hails from the Musahar community and wants a sub-quota for the marginalised SC communities. Manjhi’s son Santosh Kumar Suman, who is the Bihar minor water resources minister, has demanded a review of the country’s reservation policy to assess which sections have benefited and which have remained deprived even after 79 years of independence. The father-son duo claims they are not against reservations but want either an increase in quota or separate arrangements for sections still deprived of its benefits after seven decades.Chirag Paswan, son of Late Ram Vilas Paswan, objected to calls to introduce the “creamy layer” provision in SC/ST reservations and insisted that those advocating such a move should first resign from their positions. He stressed that the reservation policy was not based on economic status but was designed to address centuries of social discrimination, exclusion and untouchability.This is not the first time the two leaders have openly engaged in a war of words on issues.There have been instances in the past when the two Dalit leaders have openly taken diametrically opposite stands. The latest point of friction was the Bharat Tiwari encounter case of Bhojpur district. While Chirag Paswan vowed to prevail upon Bihar's BJP-led government to ensure that punishment was meted out to all police officials involved in his encounter, Manjhi asserted that police were justified in having opened fire on the 28-year-old man with an "unlicensed" weapon. Tiwari, a self-styled social and political activist, was shot dead following a heated exchange on June 17 when officials of the local administration and police visited his place to interrogate him in connection with incendiary social media posts.Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for Dalit leadership in the state. Analyst Naval Kishore Choudhary, who has observed Bihar politics for decades, says Manjhi and Paswan are engaged in a turf war."The two leaders represent two different constituencies within the SC community and are in race to establish themselves as a bigger leader within the NDA in Bihar. By taking contradictory stands, they are catering to their own constituencies within the community. There perhaps is a tussle between them to prove who is more important for NDA in Bihar," Choudhary said.However, the current issue of their discord, “quota within quota”, is not just contentious but also politically sensitive. The BJP has strategically avoided a debate on the issue of sub-quota within the Dalits, perhaps realising the uncertain fallout of any such debate.A Supreme Court judgment in August 2024, in a 6:1 majority ruling, had allowed states to sub-categorise castes within the Scheduled Castes (SC) based on socio-economic backwardness and degree of under-representation in govt jobs to ensure that the larger pie of 15% SC quota goes to the backwards among them.It had also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation. In the process, the SC overruled an earlier judgment of a five-judge bench in EV Chinnaiah case, which had said the SCs were a homogeneous group and could not be sub-categorised.The Modi government had in 2017 constituted a four-member Commission headed by Justice (Retd.) G. Rohini in October 2017 to examine the extent of inequitable distribution of benefits of reservation among the OBCs and to work out the mechanism, criteria, norms and parameters in a scientific approach for sub-categorisation within them. The Commission submitted its report to President Droupadi Murmu on July 21, 2023. However, the report has not been made public yet.Clearly, the government perhaps wants to avoid opening a Pandora’s box. More so at a time when it faces a competing challenge from the upper caste communities also. There were protests against reservations in the national capital last month, and the government engaged with the protesters. On August 21, several people held a protest in the national capital following a call by Reservation Hatao Andolan (Scrap Reservation), an Instagram-based page. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of quotas, saying that economic criteria should be given precedence over caste in determining eligibility for government support and reservation.Later, the representatives of the group held a meeting with Union minister J P Nadda and engaged in a "cordial discussion". "Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on 21 August, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Harsh Dubey, Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," Nadda said in a post on X after the meeting.Nadda's meeting with Reservation Hatao Andolan representatives drew questions from opponents. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asked Nadda to explain the Modi government's stand on the anti-reservation movement and questioned what Prime Minister Narendra Modi has to say about the August 21 protest. AAP Delhi unit president Saurabh Bharadwaj also sought clarity from Nadda on the government's position, referring to the demand for reconsideration of reservations.These political attacks notwithstanding, the BJP has to keep in mind the upper-caste sentiments. The upper caste vote has largely been with the BJP barring some exceptions, but ahead of the crucial assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh there are reports of discontent in the community.For the BJP, the challenge is two-fold. On the one hand, it has to keep the anti-reservation protesters engaged without enraging the pro-reservation groups. On the other, it has to strike a balance between competing demands of allies on sub-categorisation within the SC community.The BJP already faces pressure from the marginalised groups after stay on University Grants Commission (UGC) rules calling out caste discrimination in universities. The saffron party is also battling opposition allegations that the 2027 caste census deliberately obscures caste data. The 40 questions which are part of the census ask for many personal details, which have not so far been required for any census. However, it does not have a drop-down box for caste, nor does it ask people to self-identify as OBC to allow for proper collation of caste data.Political analyst Uday Chandra says internal conflicts within the SC community is a reality. This is more so in Bihar where Dalit identity is not totally consolidated like in other states. “The “Jati” name takes precedence over the Dalit identity in Bihar and that explains why there is a competing interest between the two Dalit leaders in the state,” Uday Chandra says.“The BJP also faces the challenge of forming new social coalitions in the runup to 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The 2014 and 2019 social coalitions which helped the BJP electorally are starting to fray and may not be effective for electoral gains,” he adds.That perhaps explains why the BJP is treading cautiously and may not be averse to the idea of “quota within quota” like it exits within the OBCs. Nitish Kumar formed the group of EBCs in Bihar and they powered his politics for years.The BJP may also ponder at the prospect of making electoral gains by prioritising the deprived within the Dalits. No wonder, the opposition parties in Bihar are already accusing the BJP of using the two ministers to test people’s mood on the issue.Bihar's leader of the opposition Tejashwi Yadav said: "The BJP is doing all this drama from behind. They are testing people's mood, putting pebbles in the water and seeing what happens." Referring to Majhi and Paswan, he said: "These people are merely characters. They only want posts. They are greedy for positions, chairs, bungalows and security, but have left society behind."Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said Union ministers making allegations against each other "goes against the Constitution". "Perhaps they do not realise that the principle of collective responsibility applies to the Council of Ministers. Whatever a minister says remains the government's position until it is contradicted," he said.But the BJP may not want to make any new experiment now as the very idea is fraught with huge political risks. Hence, to put the sparring Dalit leaders on the back foot, Bihar minister and senior BJP leader Lakhendra Paswan posed a pointed question to both the Union ministers.Without directly endorsing either position, he asked how many people from their respective communities, beyond their immediate families, they had actually helped advance. He reiterated what he described as the BJP’s position on reservation, declaring, “If there is BJP, there is reservation.” BJP national spokesperson Dr Guru Prakash Paswan also reiterated that the government has a clear stand regarding the reservation issue. "Reservation will exist till discrimination exists in society, and our government has strengthened this system. Whatever one says on this can be their personal opinion, but for social justice, the BJP is committed to fulfilling the vows of B.R. Ambedkar," he said.So, while the BJP watches its two allies in Bihar fight, it would hope that the issue does not snowball into a controversy that goes out of hand.
Article Summary: Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived Dalit sections. Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for Dalit leadership in the state.

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray on Thursday dismissed allegations linking him to the death of celebrity manager Disha Salian, questioning why he should respond to them. His remarks came after the Bombay high court directed the CBI to probe Salian’s death.Speaking to reporters, Aaditya Thackeray, the son of former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray said, "It's something that I have nothing to do about and not even thought about. Why should I even respond to this? BJP tries to defame everybody. They have tried to make Rahul Gandhi a 'Pappu' for years.”“They have tried to defame me for the last six years. Anybody who pricks the BJP, they have a problem with them. Like I said, when you have nothing to do with anything, why speak on anything or give it any importance? That's my stand..." he added.Earlier in the day, Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane said that if Thackeray and others named in connection with the case had nothing to do with Salian’s death, they should come forward and clarify their position.Rane said he had maintained from the beginning that Salian’s death should not be treated as a suicide and expressed confidence that the CBI investigation would establish the facts."We were clear from day one that this was not a suicide; this was a murder case.And events of that nature are now coming to light. Now the CBI investigation will begin, and an FIR will be lodged," Rane said.He said he expected the probe to examine allegations of evidence being destroyed and misuse of power."My only expectation is that regarding the wrong that was done to our sister named Disha Salian—the way power was misused to destroy evidence and proof—all of those things are now going to come out. In the end, no matter how much you try to hide the truth, it eventually comes out," he added.The remarks came after the Bombay high court directed the CBI to register an FIR and conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding Salian’s death. The court also directed Malvani Police Station to hand over relevant records to the CBI.The high court said no person should be treated as an accused merely on the basis of allegations made before the court.“Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless in the opinion of the investigating officer there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation,” the court said.The CBI has been asked to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to conduct the investigation.The court also said that if the probe finds that no criminal case has been made out, the CBI must file an appropriate summary report before the competent court.“In case the investigation reveals that no case is made out, then the CBI shall file the appropriate summary report before the court concerned,” it said.Salian’s father, Satish Salian, would be free to challenge such a report and file objections before the court.The high court had earlier raised concerns over the registration of only an Accidental Death Report (ADR), instead of an FIR, despite allegations made by Salian’s family. It also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to the family even years after her death.Advocate Nilesh Ojha, who represented Satish Salian, said the court had directed the CBI to record his statement and appoint a senior officer to investigate the case.The court described Salian’s father as an “unfortunate” parent who had lost his young daughter in “tragic circumstances” and said the matter required a substantive investigation. However, it did not make any adverse finding against any individual named in the allegations.Thackeray had separately approached the high court seeking to intervene in the proceedings. In his application, he described Satish Salian’s petition as “false, frivolous and motivated” and sought an opportunity to be heard before any order was passed.Salian, a celebrity manager, was found dead on June 8, 2020, after falling from a building in Mumbai. Her death occurred days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence.
Article Summary: Aaditya Thackeray dismisses allegations linking him to death of celebrity manager Disha Salian. His remarks came after the Bombay high court directed the CBI to probe Salian’s death. Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane said that if Thackery and others named in connection with the case had nothing to do with Salian's death, they should come forward.

Article Title: Cruise tourism gets a boost as govt clears e-group visa

NEW DELHI: As the govt focuses on positioning India as a leading global cruise destination, the home ministry has introduced e-group visit visa (cruise) for foreign tourists arriving in India on cruise vessels which follow a fixed and predetermined itinerary.The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The latter will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. The e-group visit visa (cruise) will have a validity of 30 days and allow multiple entry.The cruise operator or agent of the vessel will need to submit the application for e-group visit visa for international passengers via the specified portal or mobile app, three days before berthing of the vessel at the first Indian port. No fresh application will be accepted beyond this cut-off.There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e-group visit visa (cruise), home ministry sources told TOI. The details of the foreign passengers — name, nationality, passport number and issue/expiry date, etc — can be uploaded in bulk on the specified portal ( indianvisaonline.gov ) or mobile app.The e-group visit visa shall contain a QR code. Passengers may use this QR code at immigration checkpoints at the port of entry and for further travel within India, as per the fixed cruise itinerary.“Easier visa and immigration procedures will encourage international cruise companies to include Indian ports in their itineraries. This will also generate wider economic benefits for ports, hotels, restaurants, transport operators, touring businesses and local communities,” said an MHA official.The govt has, since 2024, launched two major initiatives to boost cruise tourism in India, given the great potential that the country’s 7,500-km coastline and a network of 110 navigable waterways connecting 400 rivers, presents, as per a PIB statement issued in April last year. The first initiative is Cruise Bharat Mission, launched in September 2024 with the aim of doubling the cruise traffic in India by 2029 (from 4.7 lakh in 2024 to almost 10 lakh in 2029). Also, the Maritime India Vision 2030 aims to make the country a significant player in the global cruise market, covering oceanic and coastal cruises, island and infrastructure development and river and inland cruises.
Article Summary: The nationals of all 172 countries currently eligible for e-tourist visa can avail of the dedicated e-group visit visa for cruise travel. The visa will authorise the foreign nationals arriving on cruise ships to enter India from any of the 38 designated e-visa enabled seaports. There is no limit on the number of tourists allowed on an e- group visit visa.
