BETTIAH: Unidentified and unusual fish swept into the Gandak river and its floodplains by floodwaters from Nepal have prompted the Bihar govt to issue a safety advisory, asking residents of West Champaran and Gopalganj not to consume or trade in such fish until their identity and safety are confirmed.The fisheries division of the dairy, fisheries and animal resources department issued the caution on Tuesday after unusual fish were found in local water bodies and low-lying areas across the flood-hit Gandak basin.Floodwaters from Nepal have entered the Gandak system, inundating several areas of West Champaran and Gopalganj. The department said fish can be swept away from ponds, rivers and other water bodies during floods and carried over considerable distances. During this movement, they may come into contact with contaminated drains, dead animals and other pollutants, raising the risk of contamination by bacteria, viruses and fungi.“Do not consume any unidentified or unusual-looking fish. Until confirmation by the concerned department, an unfamiliar fish should not be considered fit for consumption,” the advisory said.Residents have also been asked not to buy or sell unfamiliar fish caught from floodwaters or assume an unusual-looking species is safe merely because it resembles a commonly eaten fish.Anyone developing vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty after consuming such fish has been advised to seek immediate medical attention.Wildlife Trust of India director Sameer Kumar Sinha said most fish swept into the Gandak in Bihar following the Nepal floods are believed to be ‘Bagarius bagarius’, commonly known as the goonch catfish and locally called “Gochita”.He said the large freshwater catfish is found in fast-flowing rivers of India, Nepal and parts of Southeast Asia. The carnivorous species feeds on smaller fish, crabs and other aquatic organisms and often hides among rocks in deep stretches with strong currents.Sinha said local communities consume the fish, but it spoils quickly after death and may pose health risks if eaten after deterioration. He urged people to follow the Bihar govt advisory and exercise caution. The species is listed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) as threatened.

Article Title: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floods - what he said

Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal on Friday clarified that his statement regarding financial compensation from countries, including India, following last week's catastrophic flash floods was from the perspective of climate change and its impact in his country."Neither I nor anyone in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States," Khanal told ANI. "Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal."His clarification came after Nepal launched a diplomatic push to seek compensation from "major greenhouse gas emitters." Khanal had told local media that although the Himalayan nation contributes "virtually negligible" greenhouse gas emissions, it is bearing a "disproportionate share" of the consequences of climate change."We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create... This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability," he told Kantipur TV, excerpts of which were published by The Kathmandu Post.Meanwhile, the death toll from the Rasuwa floods had risen to 1,259 as of 7 pm Thursday, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Khanal further stressed that Nepal, India and China share the Himalayan ecosystem and face common climate risks, calling for greater regional preparedness and international support."I've also mentioned that all three countries — China, India, and Nepal face and share similar environmental ecosystems. We are all impacted by climate change in the Himalayas as well. Our call is for all these three countries to come together to be better prepared," he added, urging the global community to recognise the broader impact of rising temperatures and climate change on vulnerable communities.He also thanked India for its swift humanitarian assistance and underscored the need for regional cooperation.India was among the first countries to assist Nepal, sending emergency rescue equipment, modular bridge components, dewatering pumps, medical supplies and other relief materials. Its first relief aircraft arrived on August 26 with 10 tonnes of supplies, followed by 37.5 tonnes on August 27 and another 10-tonne consignment. A fifth aircraft later carried an 11-member rescue team, specialised equipment and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines.According to Khanal, India had remained in close contact with Kathmandu and was ready to provide further assistance as needed."In this disaster context, right after the disaster, we began to receive communication from Indian officials and they have provided all kinds of support and they have said they are standing ready to provide any support that the government of Nepal needs. We've been communicating as need arises and the government of India has fully supported our initiative. NEW DELHI: In a fresh push to curb vehicular pollution, govt will soon allow old polluting trucks and buses to be fitted with retrofit emission-control devices (RECDs) that can reduce particulate matter emissions by up to 90% and nitrogen oxide emissions by 60%. Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari announced the measure Thursday, a move that will complement govt's scrappage and replacement programme for ageing heavy vehicles.Speaking at an event organised by Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (Siam), Gadkari said the device, developed from an innovation at IIT-Delhi, has been successfully tested. Once retrofitted in BS-IV, BS-III and older diesel vehicles, it can bring their emissions on a par with BS-VI standards. Similar devices have already been installed in diesel generator sets to reduce pollution. Gadkari said each device is expected to cost around Rs 4,000-5,000.TOI has learnt that to enable the rollout, road transport ministry will soon notify Automotive Industry Standard 228, which will prescribe technical requirements and performance standards for these devices.Gadkari also highlighted India's acute shortage of buses, saying the country has only two buses per 1,000 people, compared with the global benchmark of eight.He stressed the need for innovative public transport solutions in Tier-II, Tier-III and smaller cities, arguing that metro rail projects are often too capital-intensive to be viable in such places.Taking a swipe at bureaucratic resistance, Gadkari referred to the proposed flash-charging articulated bus system in Nagpur and said, "IAS officers think they are the only intelligent people in the country. Politicians may know only how to win elections, but they believe only they have knowledge.They keep creating hurdles, but it is my responsibility to resolve them."Gadkari also reiterated his ministry's plan to introduce a negative points system for traffic violations to crack down on habitual offenders. The proposal, which he announced Wednesday while launching the 'Suraksha' pilot programme for on-the-spot medical diagnosis and counselling of 10 lakh drivers, construction workers and other high-risk workers involved in highway and mining projects, will assign penalty points for every traffic violation. Drivers accumulating points beyond a specified threshold could face suspension or cancellation of their driving licences, he said.

Article Title: Smoking raises death risk by 55% in people with diabetes, global experts call for active quit treatment
Article Text:
A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up instead of being given a one-time “quit smoking” warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses in diabetes. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Weight gain, a common concern, should not deter quitting. In a US cohort of 10,809 people with type 2 diabetes, median weight gain within six years of quitting was 3.2 kg. Long-term quitters had lower all-cause mortality than continuing smokers regardless of weight gain, with mortality hazard ratios of 0.69, 0.57 and 0.51 for no gain, up to 5 kg and more than 5 kg gain, respectively.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetes, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type 2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quit strategies and relapse prevention.The consensus also highlights gaps in diabetes care, where smoking cessation often remains limited to brief advice. It calls for routine smoking assessment, active treatment, metabolic monitoring and relapse prevention as part of diabetes care.
Article Summary: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes. A new international consensus calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up.

Article Title: SC: BCI writ runs only over lawyers, not law students
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students

Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students and quashed its letters threatening to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation.Despite BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra pleading for closure of the issue saying that the objectionable letters to the Hyderabad institute on Aug 13 were withdrawn within hours, a bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the ambit of BCI's powers, as the statutory regulatory body for the legal profession, is required to be delineated."From an in-depth consideration of the issue, we are of the opinion that Advocates Act, 1961, whereunder BCI is statutorily created, does not confer any express or implied power on BCI or state bar councils to take any disciplinary or punitive action against law students. BCI has disciplinary jurisdiction over law graduates only after they have registered as advocates," SC said.The bench agreed with senior advocate K Parameshwar who, for former Nalsar law graduate petitioners, argued that BCI does not have jurisdiction over law students, and its Aug 13 letters amounted to making deep inroads into freedom of speech and expression of students.So far as law students are concerned, it is the parent institution or the authority prescribed under laws and bylaws governing the institution who alone have the competence to take disciplinary action, if so required, against the students,” said the bench.Parameshwar said while the letter threatened to bar the registration of the Nalsar 2026 batch of law graduates as advocates, a second letter, while withdrawing the threat, directed the university to identify the students who had given the call to oppose the invitation to CJI as chief guest at the convocation. The advocate added that both letters were without jurisdiction.On Aug 14, SC stayed the operation of both letters, terming them “absolutely uncalled for”, and shielded the students and faculty ag-ainst any action by the university pursuant to BCI’s letters.BCI chief Mishra said that both letters were withdrawn subsequently.The CJI-led bench said, “Having held so, we declare all the communications of Aug 13 or subsequent modified communications to be wi-thout any authority of law.”This indictment and clipping of wings of BCI come a day after the same bench entertained petitions alleging serious irregularities in its functioning and its composition without proper elections.On Aug 14, the bench had also said BCI had nothing to do with the students’ protest against the invitation to CJI. “The students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for,” CJI had said.Trashing BCI’s threat, CJI had told Parameshwar to convey to the students “to get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court. We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.”
Article Summary: BCI threatened to debar Nalsar University law graduates from registering as advocates for opposing an invitation to CJI Surya Kant as chief guest at the institute's annual convocation. Supreme Court Thursday ruled that Bar Council of India has no jurisdiction to discipline or regulate law students. Only parent institution can take disciplinary action, says SC.

Article Title: Child sex abuse material on Meta: NHRC notices to IT, I&B ministries
Article Text:
Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta

NEW DELHI: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) as part of the ongoing scrutiny of circulation of child sexual abuse material on Instagram NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content on a platform. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said.The bench has asked whether a digital platform's legal position can continue to be treated merely as that of a passive intermediary when its systems actively generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish, amplify or monetise content.The commission has specifically asked the I&B ministry whether Meta falls within its regulatory purview as a publisher or publisher of online curated content under IT Rules, 2021 wherever the company's systems generate, modify, curate, recommend, publish or amplify content.Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.Details have also been sought regarding the regulatory status and obligations of Meta and the action required to be taken by the ministry under the existing regulatory framework.The notices to the minis-tries follow ones issued to Delhi Police in July after NHRC took cognisance of allegations concerning paid ads on Instagram that facilitated access to child sexual abuse material. The commission has now sought action taken reports within two weeks from MeitY and the I&B ministry.The matter arose after media reports by BBC World Service alleged that paid advertisements using terms such as "rape video" and "child video" were being displayed on Instagram to redirect users to Telegram channels where such material was allegedly offered for sale.The bench has also sought a response from MeitY regarding compliance with the provision on mandatory reporting of offences under Pocso Act 2012 and on whether the matter was reported to the special juvenile police unit or the local police. If not, MeitY has been asked to identify the officer or authority responsible and indicate the action taken for the lapse.Material placed before NHRC includes screenshots of Meta's systems which, according to the complainant, provide suggestions relating to content ideas, audience engagement strategies and monetisation methods.
Article Summary: National Human Rights Commission has issued notices to the ministries of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and information and broadcasting (I&B) NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on Sept 2, highlighted that the inquiry was no longer confined to who uploaded objectionable content.

Article Title: Poverty, inequality seed delinquency in minors: SC
Article Text:
The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour due to having grown up in poverty and environs marked by inequality, illiteracy and discrimination, Supreme Court has said.Exonerating a minor from the charge of attempt to erase evidence in a dowry death case, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Sh-ree Chandrashekhar traced in detail the history and development of JJ Act. They said because of industrialisation and urbanisation, rural folk migrated to cities and this weakened community cohesion, resulting in families losing control over their children.Writing the judgement, Justice Chandrashekhar said Wednesday, "Poverty, inequality, illiteracy and the discriminatory environment in which a child grows trigger delinquent behaviour... The rise in the number of cases coming to this court raising the plea of juvenility for the first time indicates in ample measure that there is a huge gap in understanding of the law by stakeholders."The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar' where they held "today's children are exposed to complex information, graphic content and adult experience that were inaccessible to the previous generation".Writing the July 21 judgement, Justice Pardiwala had analysed what propelled a person to commit a crime - "It could be enmity, it could be poverty, it could be greed, it could be perversity in mind and many others..." But the bench had not mentioned inequality, illiteracy, or a discriminatory environment as grounds for a child to turn delinquent.The bench had further said, "There is no doubt that proliferation of technology and the pervasive influence of social media has altered the cognitive and psychological development of children. In such circumstances, courts as living institutions must be responsive to this reality.""The approach of courts or the juvenile justice boards dealing with a child in conflict with the law cannot remain stagnant since the legislation came to be enacted. It must bear a balanced approach towards the evolving nature of the juvenile and legitimate demands of society," Justices Pardiwala and Bhuyan had further said.Justices Mishra and Chandrashekhar said the prosecution's eagerness to bring the culprit to court and forgetting to assess the boy's age led to overlooking of JJ Act and violation of the rights of juveniles in conflict with the law."A child should not be treated as a criminal. He is a victim of the circumstances. Sometimes he is drawn to a world of crime due to socio-economic or emotional and psychological reasons. The state owes a responsibility to reintegrate juveniles in society, rather than permanently stigmatising them," Justice Chandrashekhar said.
Article Summary: The full benefit of protective provisions of Juvenile Justice Act has not yet been extended to children who generally develop delinquent behaviour, Supreme Court has said. The order stands in stark contrast to the lengthy judgement by a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan on July 21 in the case 'X vs Bihar'

NEW DELHI: Three weeks after Lok Sabha decided to send the contentious Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a parliamentary committee for scrutiny, Speaker Om Birla Thursday named 31 members of the panel, with BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal made chairperson.BJP-led NDA's 19 MPs will be in the committee, while Congress has favoured members from minority communities as their representatives.Opposition parties, including DMK, which has split from the INDIA bloc, have been critical of the bill and supported concerns of Christian bodies that the bill's provisions will adversely impact NGOs run by them, a contention rejected by govt, even though it agreed to send the draft law for wider scrutiny to the panel to evolve a consensus.With many parties taking time in nominating their choices, the committee's constitution was held up. It has 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, and was asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of Parliament's winter session. However, a committee's tenure is often extended to allow it to engage in consultation with different stakeholders.NDA's members include Bhartruhari Mahtab, Nishikant Dubey and Tejasvi Surya of BJP, Sanjay Jha of JDU, Lavu Sri Krishna of TDP and Praful Patel of NCP.Congress MPs include Anto Antony, Viriato Fernandes, Hamdullah Sayeed and Christopher Manickam. DMK's P Wilson, a lawyer and vocal critic of the bill, is also its member besides NCP-SP's Supriya Sule and TMC's Kalyan Banerjee and Menaka Guruswamy, both lawyers.Critics' main argument against the amendment bill is that it allows the executive to take control of assets of an organisation if its FCRA license is withdrawn or not renewed.
Article Summary: BJP-led NDA's 19 MPs will be in the committee, while Congress has favoured members from minority communities as their representatives. DMK, which has split from the INDIA bloc, has been critical of the bill and supported concerns of Christian bodies that the bill's provisions will adversely impact them.

Article Title: Council can seek appraisals from teachers' institues: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday underscored the importance of the quality of teachers, who play a vital role in shaping the future of the country, and held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions (TEIs).A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense and teacher education has assumed greater importance since right to education has been recognised as a fundamental right under Right to Education Act.The bench stressed that it is necessary for the council and its bodies to ensure accountability of educational institutions. It quashed the HC order which had found fault with the council's decision to seek PAR from TEIs. "We fail to understand how a regulatory measure of a statutory body, empowered to achieve planned and coordinated development of teacher education system in the country, could be restrained from calling upon TEIs to file PAR. ...it is but natural and incidental that NCTE would require the stakeholders to provide the necessary PAR," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court held National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) can seek annual performance appraisal report (PAR) from teacher education institutions. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the role of NCTE in ensuring quality education for children is immense.

Article Title: Ladakh to have seven hill councils now, elections for new LAHDCs soon
Article Text:
All seven districts of Ladakh will now have autonomous hill development councils

SRINAGAR: All seven districts of Ladakh will now have autonomous hill development councils, with lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena approving a notification to this effect Thursday. The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts of the UT through the councils, elections to which will be held soon.So far, only Leh and Kargil districts had Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs). On July 13, the central govt announced the creation of LAHDCs for Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass districts, too. The UT administration had notified the creation of the five new districts in April this year.“The framework of elected local self-governance, which was limited to Leh and Kargil, will thereby be also extended to the five newly created districts in the UT,” a govt spokesperson said.The elections to the newly constituted councils will be held in due course after a formal notification is issued under section 8 of the LAHDC Act, 1997, the spokesperson said, adding that the notification would come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.The LAHDC-Leh was established under the LAHDC Act, 1995, while the LAHDC-Kargil was set up in 2003. Elections for both the councils are held every five years.Currently, only the LAHDC-Kargil has an elected body, as elections to its counterpart in Leh could not be held following the Sept 24 violence last year, when four people were killed after the police allegedly opened fire on protesters demanding Sixth Schedule protections and statehood for the region.In a statement here, Saxena thanked PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for the historic step, stating that the establishment of the seven councils was a milestone in strengthening grassroots governance in Ladakh, allowing local aspirations and priorities to be reflected more effectively in district-level planning and development.
Article Summary: The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts of the UT through the councils. On July 13, the central govt announced the creation of LAHDCs for Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass districts, too.

FARRUKHABAD: Uttar Pradesh Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday launched a sharp attack on previous governments, alleging that recruitment and employment opportunities for youth were earlier dominated by a "Saifai syndicate", while asserting that his government would not allow anyone to compromise with the future of young people.Addressing a gathering in Farrukhabad after distributing relief material to flood-affected families, CM Yogi said government recruitment in the state was now being carried out without discrimination."Today, for the very first time, young people are securing government jobs completely free of bias or discrimination," CM Yogi said.Targeting the previous government led by the Samajwadi Party , he alleged, "Prior to 2017, the 'Saifai syndicate' completely dominated government recruitments to the extent that no one could raise their voice. The youth remained mere spectators and were deprived of jobs."He warned those attempting to interfere with the future of the state's youth."No one will be able to do that anymore. If anyone tries to play with your future now, the doors of prison are open for them. We will send them to jail and seize their properties," CM Yogi said.The Chief Minister also highlighted schemes aimed at supporting young people, including the CM Yuva Udyami Scheme and Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Coaching facility.He said the government was also working to create employment opportunities through investment and the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector."Investment does not merely mean setting up industries; investment means employment for youth, dignity for them, and efforts directed towards making them self-reliant and independent," Yogi said.Meanwhile, CM Yogi also addressed the flood situation in Farrukhabad and assured affected families of government support, saying relief, rehabilitation and measures to find a permanent solution to recurring floods were being undertaken.He said the government would also ensure fodder, vaccinations and medicines for livestock in flood-affected areas.The development comes as several parts of Uttar Pradesh continue to monitor rising water levels in the Ganga. In Varanasi, the river was recorded at 70.54 metres at the Rajghat gauge site on Thursday morning, above the warning level of 70.262 metres.
Article Summary: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath launches attack on previous governments. Alleges recruitment and employment opportunities for youth were earlier dominated by a "Saifai syndicate" Warns those attempting to interfere with the future of the state's youth will be sent to jail.
